anti_overlap: Do not model the coupled needs/condition/health equations, or judge whether Gate 2's double-count is mathematically stable, damped, or explosive — that is fd-colonysim-deprivation-spiral's focus; take its numeric findings as given and reason only about what the player can perceive and act on.

Do not audit animal-sim's R12 vocabulary-agnosticism, the Bp fixed-point arithmetic, or whether the 18 locked decisions are architecturally coherent as engine/data boundaries — that is fd-simcore-vocab-agnosticism's focus.

Do not propose specific numeric thresholds, curves, or grace-tick values — describe what the player-facing failure mode of a proposed numeric direction would be, and leave the exact numbers to the systems-balance lens.
decision_lens: For every mechanic that claims to produce danger or drama, ask whether the player's ONE verb (dispatch) can actually intervene on it before it resolves — a threat the player cannot act on is not danger, it is weather. And for every claim that 'the spiral is the danger,' ask whether the spiral is both legible (surfaced at the interrupt tier R3's doctrine reserves for actionable trouble) and reachable (dispatch can change its outcome), not merely present somewhere in the numbers — a spiral that only ever resolves as a Toast reporting a death already happened is a eulogy, not the danger canon claims it is.
focus: Game-design review of the indirect-control/dispatch premise itself: whether the player's single verb (dispatch) can reach the failure cases the danger model creates, whether the Pause/Toast/Silent interrupt architecture and the 'vise'/no-obey-defy/breakdown-only control model still deliver felt danger and legible agency under the measured monotone, and whether the corvid-ecology grounding is honored or contradicted by where pressure actually concentrates.
name: fd-indirectcontrol-dispatch-agency
persona: Apply the perspective of a design specialist steeped in the Dwarf Fortress / RimWorld / Pikmin lineage of indirect-control, agent-dispatch simulation games — someone who has shipped or deeply studied 'you set intent, agents execute it their own way, failure is legible and actionable' systems, is fluent in Kreminski's story-sifting and Sylvester's apophenia framing (abstracted feedback plus long-term relevance as the two triggers for a felt story), and who treats 'the player has a verb' and 'the player's verb can reach the failure state' as two different claims that must each be checked separately, never inferred from each other.
review_areas: The refusal rule's site-blindness — reject_reason tests only need and condition and names no site, so AnimalCommand::Rotate cannot change a refusing bird's answer to any dispatch offer. Audit whether ANY Gate 1/2 resolution changes this, or whether 'the pause tier fires on zero idle animal-ticks' persists regardless of how health is tuned, because the structural gap is in what dispatch can target, not in how much danger exists.

Tier::Pause is reserved exclusively for SelfRefused and is the only interrupt the R3 doctrine says should take the game away from the player. Assess whether a health-centric danger model, even one that produces real deaths, would ever route through Pause at all — or whether it would only ever surface as a Toast reporting a death already resolved, i.e. whether the fix restores actionable warning or only restores a funeral notice.

Canon's 'the vise' (hunger pushes toward risk, boldness pulls back; no obey/defy, only a rare hard breakdown as loss of control) versus what is measured (132 identical heal toasts, zero refusals, zero deaths across 52 weeks) — assess whether the disposition/condition split, however mathematically sound per its own golden trajectories, is producing an experientially different game, or whether 'the numbers move but nothing legible ever happens' is itself the finding, independent of how Gate 1/2 are resolved.

The corvid-ecology reference's explicit framing of water as 'a comfort layer, not a hard timer' versus the measured reality that water is the single most-pressured need in the game (under 7000bp for 59% of the year) — if Gate 1 makes health the sole lethal path and health absorbs water deprivation, water becomes lethal-by-proxy in exactly the shape the ecology canon disclaims; assess whether that is an acceptable emergent reading or a canon violation that should be named explicitly rather than arrived at by accident of the health-routing math.

Whether 'the spiral IS the danger' (the prior goal's ruling) was ever load-bearing given the measured evidence, or whether it was an assertion the murder-loop-survive design's 'no drama director / pure emergence' premise never actually delivered on absent a working refusal → pause → dispatch loop to close it — pure emergence with no working interrupt is not RimWorld-storyteller-free drama, it is just silence.

Whether the deeper missing piece named nowhere yet is LEGIBILITY rather than raw danger — could a fully-tuned health-routing model still fail to read as danger if nothing surfaces the approach (the design doc's deferred 'named bands' question), i.e. is the gap in what happens or in what the player can see coming.
severity_examples: P0 — reject_reason's refusal loop tests only need+condition thresholds and names no site, so a refusing bird refuses every ground identically and AnimalCommand::Rotate cannot change the offer it's refusing. Because Tier::Pause fires exclusively on SelfRefused, the single player verb structurally cannot resolve the one interrupt the game reserves for actionable trouble — a real agency dead end that persists independent of any Gate 1/2 numeric fix, and should be named as its own blocker rather than assumed to resolve once refusals become non-zero.

P1 — canon's 'the vise' and 'no obey/defy, only breakdown' model depend on a felt continuum from safe to spiraling that a player experiences through repeated dispatch decisions; the measured year (0 deaths, 0 refusals, 132 identical heal-toasts) suggests the disposition/condition split, while mathematically correct against its own golden trajectories, may not yet be producing a game that FEELS different from the single-axis version it replaced — recommend distinguishing 'the numbers move' from 'the player feels the vise' as two separate acceptance bars for any Gate 1/2 fix.

P2 — water is measurably the most-pressured need (under 7000bp for 59% of the year) yet is neither lethal nor in refuse_when, while the corvid-ecology reference explicitly frames water as 'a comfort layer, not a hard timer'; if Gate 1 makes health (fed partly by water deprivation) the sole lethal path, water becomes lethal-by-proxy in exactly the way canon says it should not be — flag this tension explicitly rather than let it resolve as an unnoticed side effect of the health-routing math.
success_hints: Traces a concrete player scenario (a specific bird, a specific week, a specific rotation) through dispatch → refusal → Pause → player response, and shows explicitly where the loop currently breaks, independent of what Gate 1/2 decide about health.

For the 'what does this game most need' question, names ONE of {danger, legibility, agency, vocabulary-structure} as the primary diagnosis, with the measured evidence that subordinates the other three — rather than listing all four as equally plausible and declining to choose.
Distinguishes a genuinely DF-faithful 'silent decay then spiral' texture from a system that merely has the right formula shape but never surfaces or resolves through play.

Delivers a direct, adversarial verdict on whether 'the spiral IS the danger' still holds, citing the specific measured counter-evidence (0 refusals, 0 deaths, 132 identical toasts, zero idle-animal-ticks satisfying the refusal conjunction) rather than accepting the prior ruling's framing at face value.
task_context:
Apply an indirect-control / agent-dispatch game-design lens to the following review target.

Review two things together. (1) THE PROPOSED GOAL, drafted this session and pending mk's sign-off, at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-sma-projects/f8f5d301-b169-47b0-8a4a-116a5a5b7ec9/scratchpad/goal.txt — 'deprivation reaches health, and the year can hurt me'. Its premise: food and water deprivation should damage health, health becomes the accumulator every hardship routes through, and health becomes (probably) the sole lethal need. Two open gates: does food stay lethal, and is the condition double-count (deficits pull condition directly AND via health) the intended death spiral or does one path get damped. (2) THE GAME DESIGN OVERALL — docs/ravenous-vision.md is the spine (18 locked decisions), plus docs/design-2026-06-20-murder-loop-survive.md, docs/design-2026-07-24-needs-availability-and-condition.md, docs/reference-2026-06-20-corvid-ecology.md, docs/design-2026-06-20-df-feel-depth.md, docs/reference-2026-06-30-genre-influences.md. RaveNous is an indirect-control civic sim: you command a murder of named, personality-driven ravens tending a procedurally-generated city, DNA of Dwarf Fortress x Factorio x SimCity x The Sims x Heart of the Machine. Rust workspace: animal-sim (deterministic, VOCABULARY-AGNOSTIC needs/assignment substrate, ruling R12 — must run an octopus game unchanged, enforced by scripts/check-agnosticism.sh) + raven-vocab (all raven content as pure data) + ravenous-session + ravenous-readout + ravenous-app (Bevy). KEY MEASURED CONTEXT, all committed this session: a shipped 52-week year produces ZERO deaths, ZERO arrivals, ZERO refusals, and 132 identical toasts — the surface has a monotone. Probe crates/ravenous-session/src/bin/how_close_is_it.rs at tick resolution found food floors at 1076/10000, water at 1837 (under 7000 for 59% of the year), health at 9810 (never below 9000 all year), interest at 8250, condition at 0 for 4.5% of ticks. Three causes: (a) health is one of two lethal needs but its recovery is ungated while its only loss is night-gated, so it is pinned at the ceiling; (b) death requires a lethal need at EXACTLY zero for 40 consecutive ticks, a cliff with no gradient into it; (c) the refusal rule is a conjunction of a common condition (986 animal-ticks/yr) and a near-impossible one (13), satisfied on ZERO idle animal-ticks against a 16% idle base rate. The one need under real pressure (water) is neither lethal nor in refuse_when. WHAT I WANT FROM THIS REVIEW: is routing all deprivation through health the right architecture, or is there a better model we are not seeing? What does this game most need that nobody has named — is the real gap danger, or legibility, or player agency, or something structural about the vocabulary-agnostic split? Are the 18 locked decisions still serving the game, or is one of them the thing holding it back? Interrogate the pace-layer/indirect-control premise hard: the player's only verb is dispatch, and we just measured that a refusing bird refuses every ground alike so dispatch cannot reach the one case the pause tier fires on. Be adversarial about whether 'the spiral IS the danger' (last goal's ruling) was ever true.
